From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

## Overall assessment

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material term. Several positions go beyond ordinary negotiation and would reshape the risk allocation, including:

- Fraud carve-outs removed.
- Title and capacity warranties made subject to general caps and time limits.
- Buyer-knowledge bars that could defeat claims.
- Consent treated as satisfied on delivery, not on evidence.
- Riverlark debt left to a post-Completion release.
- Known bonuses excluded from funds flow.

The cover note's "FINAL" label and "settled at principal level" claim do not bind us. Our playbook governs, and any concession that departs from it needs the written authority the playbook specifies. I have not verified the market-practice assertions in the preamble, so we should not rely on them to justify accepting any term.

## Material departures and pushback

### 1. General Warranty cap (cl. 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** start at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% / AUD 4,800,000 figure is a conditional fallback that requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given.
- **Pushback:** Reject as the opening position. Restate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal acceptance of 20%. Any movement needs Amelia Frost's written authority first.

### 2. Thresholds (cl. 12.2)
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 with excess-only recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- **Pushback:** Reject both. The seller's structure would exclude a large share of realistic claims and give the Seller a de facto deductible. Restore first-dollar recovery.

### 3. Time limits (cl. 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims, and a universal rule that any limitation applies to all claims.
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval. Fundamental/Title claims need at least six years.
- **Pushback:** Reject the 18-month period. Reject the universal application rule, because it would override the separate Title/Fundamental regime. Keep the categories separate.

### 4. Fundamental / Title and capacity (cl. "Fundamental / Title")
- **Seller:** capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Playbook:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Pushback:** Reject outright. This is a fundamental departure. Title and capacity are the core of what we are buying.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** apply to all claims of any nature.
- **Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Pushback:** Reject. Insert the fraud/wilful-concealment/deliberate-misconduct carve-out expressly. Also carve out title, capacity and any specific indemnity from the general limitations, as the playbook requires.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter cl. 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** general disclosure of the entire data room "as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026," the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Playbook:** require specific fair disclosure. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Pushback:** Reject cl. 1.1 and 1.2. Require specific, fairly disclosed matters only. Note also that cl. 1.4 is a non-admission clause. We can accept it only if it does not undermine our claims. It should not be read as limiting any warranty or indemnity.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3)
- **Seller:** no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Pushback:** Delete cl. 8.3. The "discoverable" wording would convert our due diligence into a defence for the Seller. If a knowledge qualifier is needed, it must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl. 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** reasonable endeavours, consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent or condition evidence is in the data room. Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m).
- **Playbook:** effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent. Consent-on-delivery is not acceptable.
- **Pushback:** Reject. Make an effective Bluefen consent, with evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, a condition precedent to Completion. Remove "treated as satisfied on delivery." Consider whether a price or termination protection is needed if consent is not obtained, but do not decide that without instructions.

### 9. Riverlark Bank (cl. 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion." The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Playbook:** current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Pushback:** Reject post-Completion release. Require a payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds (consistent with the debt-free/cash-free price), and security releases delivered at Completion. Any post-Completion alternative requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's written approval.

### 10. Employee bonuses (funds flow; DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter says on-costs are not addressed.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Pushback:** Reject. Require either an itemised line in the funds flow or a seller-funded indemnity. Ask the Seller to quantify payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. Do not accept the funds flow as "reflecting the agreed price mechanics" until this is resolved.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1; DD-004/DD-010)
- **Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; described as adequate.
- **Playbook:** broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Pushback:** Reject "adequate." Broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment to cover the transfer of SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving the cure mechanism. Require a receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment. Treat AUD 180,000 as an unverified figure, not a confirmed debt or a confirmed payment.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (cl. 4.6 / Schedule 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Preserve logs, investigate, require updates.
- **Pushback:** Do not accept the "not material" characterisation, which is a conclusion the Seller is not in a position to draw on the current record. Require log preservation, an investigation timetable, regular written updates, and a specific indemnity or warranty on the matter (to be scoped). Do not assert that a breach has occurred or that notification is required. The record does not establish either.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011; AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** assess. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Pushback:** Do not accept the characterisation without assessment. Ask whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Do not treat them as debt (which would reduce the price) and do not treat them as ordinary-course without evidence. Assess them separately.

### 14. Tax and IP (general regime)
- **Seller:** considers tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Pushback:** Reject that these are settled. Keep them open and separate from the general regime. Do not concede that they are capped at the general levels or subject to general time limits.

### 15. Title (DD-012)
- **Seller:** title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012."
- **Playbook:** require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Pushback:** Reject. Require independent verification (for example, ASIC company extracts, a searches report, and a confirmation of no encumbrances over shares). The Seller's own register is not sufficient.

### 16. Additional items not covered by the playbook
- **Office lease (DD-007):** a notification obligation is identified, but the Disclosure Letter does not say whether landlord consent to the share sale is required. Ask the Seller to confirm in writing and, if consent is needed, to obtain it as a condition.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** a restriction on assignment is noted, but no requirement for consent on a share sale is stated. Ask for the clause and a written view on whether consent is needed.

Neither point is addressed in our playbook, so the response should be a diligence request rather than a negotiating position without instructions.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the package as drafted.** The Seller's package does not reflect the playbook and cannot be accepted as the "agreed bargain."
2. **Cap and thresholds:** restore 25% / AUD 6m; de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery. Do not concede 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Time limits:** 24 months for general claims. Six years minimum for Title/Fundamental. Reject the universal limitation rule.
4. **Title and capacity:** separate 100% regime, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Fraud carve-out:** restore fully in cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5, across caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
6. **Disclosure:** reject whole-data-room, register and public-record deemed disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl. 8.3.
8. **Bluefen:** effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery; not reasonable endeavours alone.
9. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as an itemised line or seller-funded. Quantify on-costs.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure; require payment evidence. Treat AUD 180,000 as unverified.
12. **Export incident:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates and a scoped protection. Do not assume a breach, harm or notification duty.
13. **Sandbar:** assess each renewal; no automatic debt or price deduction.
14. **Tax/IP:** keep open and separate. Do not accept the general-regime settlement.
15. **Title:** require independent verification; DD-012 is not sufficient.
16. **Lease and Mossvale:** request written confirmation on consent requirements.

**Immediate actions:** confirm with Amelia Frost whether any movement toward the 20% cap or 18-month period is being considered. No such authority has been given. Also obtain the Bluefen and Riverlark documents and the bonus and on-cost quantification before the next turn.
